title: Performance With One Bleed Source Unavailable
abstract: Flight crew performance information for operation with one bleed source unavailable, covering the take-off and climb penalties, the maximum operating altitude and the cabin altitude consequence.

sections.purpose: Gives the flight crew the performance consequences of operating with one bleed source unavailable, for dispatch planning and for an in-flight loss.
sections.description: Loss of a bleed source reduces the air available for air conditioning and pressurisation and, where the loss occurs before take-off, changes the take-off performance because the remaining source must carry a larger extraction. The take-off weight penalty is tabulated against outside air temperature and pressure altitude and is significant at high and hot airfields, where it can be the limiting factor rather than the runway length. In the climb the maximum operating altitude is reduced, and above the tabulated level the cabin altitude will rise beyond the normal schedule with one source. Where the loss occurs in flight the crew should expect the cabin altitude to stabilise higher than usual and should plan the descent profile accordingly. A shutdown that has occurred without a confirmed cause is treated the same way as a genuine loss for performance purposes; the crew have no means of distinguishing the two and must not assume the source will return.
sections.crew_procedure: For dispatch, apply the take-off weight penalty for the outside air temperature and pressure altitude at the departure airfield, and confirm the reduced maximum operating altitude against the planned route. In flight, on loss of a source, level off at or below the reduced maximum operating altitude and monitor the cabin altitude. Plan the descent to arrive at a level consistent with the remaining source. Do not assume a source that has shut down without an evident cause will return.
sections.limitation_note: Maximum operating altitude with one bleed source unavailable: as tabulated, below the normal maximum. Take-off weight penalty: as tabulated against outside air temperature and pressure altitude. Cabin altitude will stabilise above the normal schedule at the upper end of the reduced envelope.

type_data.crew_action: Apply the take-off weight penalty and the reduced maximum operating altitude; monitor cabin altitude.
